title: Rajasthan Heritage Itinerary: Forts, Palaces and Old Cities in 10 to 14 Days
seoTitle: Rajasthan Heritage Itinerary: 14 Days of Forts & Palaces | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: A 14-day Rajasthan heritage itinerary: Jaipur, Ranthambore, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Udaipur, Kumbhalgarh and Ranakpur, Jodhpur and Jaisalmer, with drive times and tips.
description: A 14-day Rajasthan heritage itinerary through forts, palaces and old cities: Jaipur and Amber, Ranthambore's fort and tigers, Bundi's stepwells and murals, Chittorgarh, Udaipur's lakes and City Palace, Kumbhalgarh and the Ranakpur temple, Jodhpur's Mehrangarh and Jaisalmer's living fort, with drive times, where to break the journey and shorter versions.
dek: Rajasthan rewards a slow road trip, from the pink city of Jaipur to the golden fort of Jaisalmer. This two-week route covers the best of its forts, palaces and old towns.

hero.alt: The gateway and walls of Jaisalmer Fort

intro: Rajasthan is India's best-known heritage state, with four UNESCO sites (the Hill Forts of Rajasthan, Jaipur's walled city, the Jantar Mantar and Keoladeo National Park) and dozens of forts, palaces and havelis. The distances are large, so a car and driver is the easiest way to travel.

This 14-day route starts in Jaipur and ends in Jaisalmer, from where you can fly or take a train back, or continue to Bikaner and Delhi. It includes all six of the UNESCO hill forts except remote Gagron, which can be added from Bundi.
quickAnswer: A 14-day Rajasthan heritage itinerary: Jaipur (2 nights), Ranthambore (2), Bundi (1), Chittorgarh (1), Udaipur (3, with a day at Kumbhalgarh and Ranakpur), Jodhpur (2) and Jaisalmer (2), then fly or take a train onward. Travel by car and driver, and go between October and March. Shorter versions can drop Ranthambore and Bundi.
takeaways: Two weeks lets you see Rajasthan's great forts and cities without rushing.
A car and driver is the most practical way to travel.
Five of the six UNESCO hill forts are on this route.
Udaipur makes a good mid-trip rest stop.
October to March is the season; desert nights are cold in December and January.

rows: Amber Fort, City Palace, Jantar Mantar, Hawa Mahal
City Palace, Lake Pichola; day trip to Kumbhalgarh and Ranakpur
Fly or train from Jaisalmer or Jodhpur

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: Rajasthan is the best place in India to stay in heritage hotels: havelis in Jaipur, Bundi and Jaisalmer, palace hotels in Udaipur and Jodhpur, and fort stays near Kumbhalgarh. They range from simple family-run guesthouses to luxury palaces. In Jaisalmer, staying outside the fort walls helps reduce the strain on the old fort's drainage and structure. Book the winter months, especially Christmas and New Year, well ahead.

sections.heading: Keeping the pace comfortable
list: Break long drives with stops: Ranakpur between Udaipur and Jodhpur, or Osian between Jodhpur and Jaisalmer.
Plan one slow day in Udaipur to rest.
Start fort visits at opening time; afternoons are hot even in winter.
Use evenings for markets, folk shows and rooftop dinners.

sections.heading: Beyond the monuments
list: The block printers of Sanganer and Bagru near Jaipur.
Bagore ki Haveli's evening dance show in Udaipur.
The Rajasthan International Folk Festival at Mehrangarh, usually in October.
Desert villages and the Jaisalmer Desert Festival in February.

sections.heading: Tips
list: Agree the full route, overnight stops and driver's accommodation when you book a car.
Carry a scarf and hat; the sun is strong in forts.
Keep some cash; small towns and fort stalls may not take cards.

safety: Timings, closures and train schedules change; check the ASI, state tourism and IRCTC before you go.
Driving times are approximate; allow extra time, and avoid long drives after dark.
Desert nights are cold in winter; carry warm layers.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Rajasthan?
faqs.a: Ten to fourteen days for the main heritage cities; a week for a shorter loop.

faqs.q: What is the best route for Rajasthan?
faqs.a: Jaipur, Ranthambore, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Udaipur, Jodhpur and Jaisalmer, in that order, is a logical loop.

faqs.q: Is it better to travel by car or train?
faqs.a: A car and driver is easier for forts and small towns; trains work between the big cities.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Rajasthan?

faqs.a: Yes, between Jaipur and Jodhpur, or from Ajmer.
